Subject: Demo request: Dedicated capacity (throughput/latency)

Hi Marissa,

I signed up through the self-serve flow yesterday and indicated interest in Redwood Dedicated for a production use case. We're Olive AI — building clinical automation — and need a demo focused on Dedicated capacity: specifically throughput targets and p99 latency at scale.

High-level requirements:
- Peak concurrent requests: ~120 concurrent streams
- Avg tokens per request: 1.2k tokens (generation + context)
- Target p50 latency: <150ms per token, p99 under 600ms
- Preferred models: open variants compatible with Redwood (we're testing Llama2-70B and other opt-in weights)

Can we schedule a 30–45 minute call this week to walkthrough Dedicated capacity sizing, kernel/quantization tradeoffs, and typical autoscaling profiles? Please include someone technical who can speak to batching/options for improving throughput.

Thanks,
Andrew
Andrew Ho
Head of Platform
Olive AI

Thanks for the add — looping in Connor (SE) as well for kernel/quantization examples.

Quick notes so we can make the call concrete:
- For ~120 concurrent streams at ~1.2k tokens/request we typically recommend Dedicated pools sized for sustained RPS and headroom for bursts; rough starting point is 8x A100-equivalent GPUs with model quantization (4-bit) depending on model family.
- Batch size: we tune to target per-GPU throughput; batching increases latency variance but improves throughput. We'll show p50/p95/p99 examples from similar customers.
- Autoscale: policy-based on queue length + headroom; for your burstiness we usually set a lower threshold for scale-up to preserve p99.

Connor will prepare a short sizing slide and a small throughput test plan (staging endpoint + simple load generator) if you want to validate.

ADDITIONAL: I have a conflict Wed 3pm — can we move to Thu Mar 12 at 11:00am PDT? If that works for you, Connor and I will be available.

- Aditya
